text:
Ottawa arrives as the better team on the underlying numbers. The Senators have taken 47% of the five-on-five expected goals this season, while Philadelphia sits at 35%, and the Flyers allow 3.70 expected goals per 60 against Ottawa's 2.79. The model projects 3.13 expected goals for OTT tonight to 2.50 for PHI. On special teams, OTT's power play (0.87 expected goals a game) tops PHI's (0.55), though the Senators take 4.75 penalties a game, which keeps feeding opposing power plays. PHI's penalty kill allows 0.72 expected goals a game to Ottawa's 0.68.

In net, projected starters Linus Ullmark (OTT) and Dan Vladar (PHI) have gone opposite directions. Ullmark is +7.59 goals saved above expected this season with a .949 save percentage, and he was -13.3 last year. Vladar is -2.56 this season at .875 after a +12.74 year in 2025-26. Recent form tells the same story: OTT is 4-1-0 in its last five with 50% of the expected goals, while PHI is 0-4-1 with 43%. The Flyers are winless in nine (0-6-3), outscored 33-11, and the chances say it's real, at 37% of the expected goals. Ottawa won the first meeting 2-1 on Oct 8, a game it deserved 30% of the time.

Tim Stützle is the Senators' best bet at 35% to score and 72% to record a point, though he's flagged as due to cool. Drake Batherson (32% to score) leads the Ottawa power play. For Philadelphia, Trevor Zegras is at 22% to score and 49% for a point, and Matvei Michkov is one goal from 50 career goals. Both teams are missing key forwards, Travis Konecny for PHI and William Eklund for OTT.
